verdicts.strongest_argument: The pattern is real -- I verified 424B3s on 2025-08-12, 2025-09-29, 2025-11-06 and 2026-03-24, and the 2026-03-24 supplement's own text says it supplements the 20-June-2025 prospectus 'with the information contained in our report on Form 6-K, filed with the SEC on March 24, 2026' for 11,080,332 BRPC II shares; the 2025-11-06 supplement says the same for a 6-K filed 2025-11-06, and a POS AM followed the Q1 print by two days. But the fact is published on a retail-facing filing-summary site on each of those days (StockTitan carried '11,080,332 common shares for resale by B. Riley Principal Capital II' on 2026-03-24 and 'registers 11.08M shares; $20M equity facility noted' on 2026-05-29), and the POS AM itself already draws out the dilution-to-float implication verbatim: the shares 'would represent approximately 15.8% of the total number of outstanding Common Shares and approximately 58.6% of the total number of outstanding Common Shares held by non-affiliates.' So the size relative to float is the issuer's own disclosed sentence, not a discovery. More damaging is the flow: the supplements disclose cumulative ELOC usage of 201,682 shares at 2025-09-30 and 215,272 at 2025-12-31 -- about 13,590 shares drawn in all of Q4 2025, 0.02% of shares outstanding per quarter. A prospectus supplement incorporating results is mandatory housekeeping to keep any resale registration usable; it is not a supply event, and management has said it deliberately did not draw at ~$1.27. What survives is narrow but genuine: nobody has published that the earnings 6-K is the mechanical trigger, and nobody has connected the refreshed-effective shelf to the fact that spot at $1.38 now clears the CEO's own stated reservation price. That inference is unpublished and reaches tomorrow.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The rate data is not merely public, it is the single most-covered story in shipping this quarter. Frontline printed a record Q2 on 2026-08-28 with VLCC TCE of $152,700/day, Lloyd's List called the 2026 tanker boom the second-best in history on the same week, Teekay reported near-record midsize rates, and the trade press has noted this is the fourth consecutive quarter of six-figure VLCC earnings -- so the sequential step-up is an increment inside a boom already running four quarters, not a regime change. Heidmar's own leverage to it is also pre-narrated: the CEO told Capital Link on 2026-02-19 the company is 'a proxy for the tanker market' with earnings responding directly to freight through management fees and revenue-sharing, and quoted VLCCs at ~$120,000/day. The sell-side has already revised up -- Maxim's Tate Sullivan raised FY2026 and FY2027 revenue and EBITDA after the Q1 print and lifted the target to $2.25, 63% above spot. Most decisively, the tape: HMR went $1.11 on 2026-08-03 to $1.45 on 2026-08-20 and $1.38 on 08-31, and that window is exactly the tanker peer reporting season. The +24.33% 20-day run-up is the read-through being paid for. The genuinely obscure part is only the arithmetic -- that a two-analyst FY2026 revenue print of $74.29m backs into ~$18.6m quarters -- and I could not locate that number published anywhere, but a two-analyst consensus on a foreign-private-issuer de-SPAC is not the price-setting benchmark: Q1 missed the revenue 'consensus' by 32% and the stock has since risen roughly 25% off the low. Note also that most of the sequential revenue swing sits in the $12.67m voyage-and-time-charter line, which is gross freight on chartered-in tonnage with hire cost against it, so a large revenue beat does not translate proportionally to net income.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I think this one is largely a category error rather than a discovery. Q-Shipping B.V. is a ship-management and crewing business and the nine vessels it brought are 'a mix of bulk carriers, general cargo vessels, and chemical/product tankers' -- those belong in TECHNICAL management, not the commercial pool count the 20-F's '49 vessels' refers to. The published series bears that out: Capital Link 2026-02-19 quotes 'about 40 tankers under commercial management and 10 under technical management'; the 2026-07-07 release says 'around 50 under commercial management and 16 under technical management.' Technical went 10 to 16 across the period that contains the acquisition. Total managed therefore went from 49-50 to ~66, an increase of roughly a third, not 'effectively flat.' Second, the 49-versus-50 gap the claim leans on is rounding inside a single document: the same 20-F fleet table (5 VLCC, 9 Suezmax, 4 LR2, 2 LR1, 11 MR, 7 Aframax, 3 small, 1 PSV, 5 bulkers, 3 broker) is described by screeners as '50 vessels as of April 30, 2026.' Third, the claim's own supporting assertion -- 'no fleet-addition press release since 2026-05-19' -- is contradicted by the 2026-07-07 release it cites in the same sentence. Fourth, sizing: pool and management fees are a minority of an $18.4m quarter, and a plus-or-minus-four swing in commercial vessel count is a rounding error against a 47-82% sequential rate move. What is unpriced is only the negative inference itself, which nobody has drawn -- because it is probably not true.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The departure is wire copy, not a discovery. GlobeNewswire on 2026-06-01, then Investing.com, TradeWinds ('Heidmar hunts new finance chief as Niki Fotiou leaves after three years'), StockTitan, TipRanks/theFly, GuruFocus, Manila Times and Yahoo all carried it inside 24 hours, including the detail that Khanna would oversee the finance function pending a search. That no successor has been named is verifiable by anyone in ten seconds from the empty news record -- Heidmar has issued exactly four press releases between 2026-06-01 and 2026-08-31 -- so 'Q2 is the first quarter closed without a CFO' is an inference that requires no work and confers no informational edge. The 'no 6-K since 2026-05-28' half I confirmed on EDGAR, but it does not support the reading placed on it: a foreign private issuer is not required to furnish a 6-K for every press release, and all three subsequent items were press-released and wire-covered, so nothing was withheld from the market. What is left is a genuine but small residual -- elevated risk of a delayed or thin release, or a weaker MD&A, on a print where the date has already been company-confirmed for 2026-09-01 pre-open.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The premise is refuted. The claim rests on 'every screener reports the 59m count' as float; both of the most-used free screeners report the small float, and report it smaller than the prospectus does. stockanalysis.com shows shares outstanding 58.99m, float 6.07m, insider ownership 89.71%, institutions 0.40%; finviz shows Shs Outstand 58.99M, Shs Float 5.53M, Insider Own 90.62%. So a ~10% float is on the free web, not buried in a POS AM. The prospectus quote itself is accurate -- I read p12151143_pos-am.htm and it says verbatim 'As of May 20, 2026, we had 58,991,997 Common Shares outstanding, of which 6,498,572 shares were held by non-affiliates of our company' -- but the number it produces is larger than what the screeners already publish, so the finding, if acted on, corrects the price in the wrong direction. Separately, this is a width fact and not a directional one, and the width is already in the baseline: 71.9% annualised realised vol on 50,189 shares a day and a 5.13% median print reaction are exactly what a 5-6m share float on an $83m de-SPAC produces. Finally the brief's short-interest figure of 127,609 shares is not confirmed by either screener (53,874 and ~50,000).

verdicts.strongest_argument: The documents check out -- I read two of the three primary_doc.xml files directly (Loutradis 126,575 shares, $138,699, broker Piraeus Securities S.A., sale date 2026-06-26, of which 104,954 were an employee stock award dated 2026-04-01; Lockhorst 5,000 shares, $5,950, sale date 2026-07-08, board compensation acquired 2025-07-18) -- but the finding fails on both publication and timing. And the mechanism does not reach tomorrow: the stated sale dates were in June and July, the Rule 144 windows from those filings are expired or nearly so, and whatever selling occurred passed through the tape during a period in which the stock rose from $1.11 to $1.38. Two smaller points: the 3.8% figure uses the 6,498,572 denominator that h1#4 supplies, and both screeners put the float below that, so the true percentage is nearer 4.4%; and Loutradis received employee stock awards, so describing all three sellers as 'directors' is loose.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component is published, and the most important one was pre-announced by management. The concentration is the 20-F's own related-party disclosure -- 'The Capital vessels compose 25 of the 49 vessels currently managed by Heidmar' and 'accounted for 37% of our total revenues from the Pools during the year ended December 31, 2025', with Capital owned by the father of the indirect owner of Maistros Shipinvest, a Heidmar major shareholder -- filed 2026-04-30 and summarised by StockTitan the same week. The Capital Tankers listing was not obscure: Euronext's own press release called the NOK 4.8bn / ~USD 500m placement 'the largest western shipping listing in the last two decades' on 2026-03-17, and it was covered by MarketScreener, elnavi and the shipping trades. Crucially, the CEO had already told investors on 2026-02-19 to expect 'roughly 30 newbuilding vessels to enter its platform over the next two years' -- that is the Capital Tankers pipeline, disclosed a month before the listing. And the direction is ambiguous: the same fact is a customer-concentration risk and a funded newbuild pipeline flowing into Heidmar's pools. Nothing here lands inside a Q2 print: 21 of the 30 vessels are newbuildings delivering 2026-2028, so the fee impact is quarters and years out, not tomorrow morning.

adversary_notes: Three factual problems worth flagging, one of them decisive. (1) h1#4's premise is wrong. Its force comes from the contrast between a hidden 11% float in a POS AM and screeners that supposedly show 59m. Both major free screeners show the small float and show it smaller than the prospectus: stockanalysis.com reports float 6.07m / insider own 89.71%, finviz reports Shs Float 5.53M / Insider Own 90.62%. The verbatim prospectus quote is accurate -- I read the document -- but it is less bearish than what is already on the free web. The brief's short interest of 127,609 shares is also unconfirmed; the screeners show 53,874 and ~0.05m. (2) h1#2 compares non-comparable categories. Q-Shipping is a ship-management and crewing business and its nine vessels (bulkers, general cargo, chemical/product tankers) belong in technical management, which the public series shows going 10 (Feb 2026, Capital Link) to 16 (Jul 2026 release), while commercial went ~40 to ~50 over the same period. Total managed rose from 49-50 to ~66. The claim also asserts 'no fleet-addition press release since 2026-05-19' while citing a 2026-07-07 fleet-addition press release. (3) h1#0's sub-claim of 'two 424B3s the day after the 2025-08-11 print' is wrong: EDGAR shows one 424B3 on 2025-08-12 (0000919574-25-004444); the other accession the brief appears to be counting, 0000919574-25-004078, is dated 2025-07-11. That is cosmetic -- the underlying pattern is real and I verified it at four dates, including that the 2025-11-06 supplement incorporates a 6-K filed 2025-11-06, which my initial 6-K list had missed. Where I concede: h1#0's core mechanism is documented, unpublished as a mechanism, and reaches tomorrow -- and it supplies a causal story for a reaction history (5 of 6 prints down, median 5.13% absolute) that the baseline measured and then discarded with history_usable=0. Rehabilitating that history is the most valuable thing in this brief. The sharpest unpublished detail anywhere in it is not in the brief's own framing: the CEO declined to draw the equity line at ~$1.27 as not reflective of value, spot is now $1.38, and 2026-09-01 is the first print under a shelf re-declared effective on 2026-06-11 (EFFECT filing; the brief says 2026-06-10, a one-day discrepancy). On the name overall: with no option chain there is no priced direction to argue against, so 'already in the price' here has to mean 'already in the public record and plausibly in the +24.33% twenty-day run-up.' That run-up maps cleanly onto the tanker peer reporting window (Aug 3 $1.11 to Aug 20 $1.45), which is why I put h1#1 at 68 rather than lower despite being unable to find the $74.29m consensus figure published anywhere.
